facts.fact: Rohan's writ is a folded creamy paper with red wax, carried in a boiled-leather writ case stamped with a goat. Meera cuts a strip from the case to make snow goggles, and Rohan moves the paper inside his coat.
facts.why: needed because the beat has her cut goggle slits from a strip of leather from his writ case.

facts.fact: Asha's crew is recognisable by packs covered in onion-skin ochre canvas.
facts.why: needed because Meera must identify the distant pairs as Asha's crew.

facts.fact: The crew ledge is a shelf cut by Bindu's mother forty winters ago into the cornice on the south face, with iron pegs and a cache of three days' food and two dry blankets. It is reached across a gully with an eight-pace snow bridge.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires a hidden crew ledge and a snow bridge that fails.

facts.fact: Rohan tells Meera that he carries a thing the regent's side would pay a lordship for, and that he believes the four pursuers have been told where to find him. He declines to name it.
facts.why: needed for the beat in which he admits carrying something valuable without saying what.
